findings.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with a raw Integer instead of the established group.remove(user) pattern used by add_members (line 73); empirically reproduced with this environment's activerecord 4.1.16/arel 5.0.1 (has_many :through) this raises TypeError: Cannot visit Integer, so the endpoint 500s in production even though it bypasses whatever bookkeeping Group#remove performs

app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — {{#unless automatic}}` inside the per-member itemView resolves against the loop item's context (the member/User object), not the parent Group, since no itemController is used; `automatic` is not a User attribute, so it evaluates to undefined and the remove ("x") link is shown for every group including automatic groups, contrary to the evident intent of hiding member removal for automatic groups (server still rejects the deletion, but combined with the silent-failure bug above the admin gets a dead control with no explanation)

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:88 — xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "..."` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` invoke the controller action directly via a params hash and never resolve through config/routes.rb, so these specs would still pass even if the route definitions in config/routes.rb were wrong; verified empirically with actionpack 4.1.16 that the current bare `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` / `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` declarations inside `resources :groups do ... end` do correctly nest as `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`, matching group.js's `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json` calls, so the route itself is NOT currently broken, but the test suite provides no safety net against a future regression in that route wiring

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with a raw Integer instead of the established group.remove(user) pattern used by add_members (line 73); empirically reproduced with this environment's activerecord 4.1.16/arel 5.0.1 (has_many :through) this raises TypeError: Cannot visit Integer, so the endpoint 500s in production even though it bypasses whatever bookkeeping Group#remove performs

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does call `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an Integer, while `add_members` uses the higher-level `group.add(user)` API. This inconsistency is real and could bypass any bookkeeping/callbacks that `Group#remove` might implement (not shown in the diff). However, the claimed runtime `TypeError: Cannot visit Integer` and resulting 500 cannot be verified from the diff alone (and a new spec exercises `remove_member` successfully), so the “will 500 in production” assertion isn’t provable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — {{#unless automatic}}` inside the per-member itemView resolves against the loop item's context (the member/User object), not the parent Group, since no itemController is used; `automatic` is not a User attribute, so it evaluates to undefined and the remove ("x") link is shown for every group including automatic groups, contrary to the evident intent of hiding member removal for automatic groups (server still rejects the deletion, but combined with the silent-failure bug above the admin gets a dead control with no explanation)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs` the members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, which creates a per-item view whose template (`admin/templates/group_member.hbs`) is evaluated in the item/view context, not the parent group/controller context. The `group_member.hbs` template gates the remove link with `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}`, but `automatic` is a group attribute (used correctly in `group.hbs`), not a `Discourse.User`/member attribute, so in the per-member context it will be undefined/falsey and the `unless` will pass—showing the “remove” control even for automatic groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:40 — update` silently no-ops a name change on automatic groups (`if params[:name] && !group.automatic`) while sibling actions `add_members`/`remove_member` use an explicit `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic` guard that renders a 422 — the inconsistent style leaves future readers unsure whether "can't modify automatic group" should be a silent skip or an explicit rejection

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: `Admin::GroupsController#update` sets `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic`, so a rename request on an automatic group is silently ignored while still allowing other fields (e.g., `visible`) to be updated, and the comment explicitly says “group rename is ignored for automatic groups”. In contrast, the newly added membership endpoints `add_members` / `remove_member` both do `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic` and return a 422. This is a real, diff-grounded consistency/semantics concern (API behavior differs between endpoints) but not a clear functional defect since the silent skip is explicitly coded and tested (`spec ... ignore name change on automatic group`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:106 — // TODO: should clear the input` left in `addMembers` action with no tracking issue or follow-up — a dead-end TODO that will likely never get done

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an `addMembers` action containing the comment `// TODO: should clear the input`, but the finding’s claim that it has “no tracking issue or follow-up” and is a “dead-end TODO that will likely never get done” is not verifiable from the PR diff and is speculative rather than a concrete, diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public `members` action's `limit` param has no upper bound clamp, so a caller can request an arbitrarily large page (mild resource-exhaustion risk); low impact since non-automatic groups were previously returned unbounded anyway and access is already gated by `guardian.ensure_can_see!

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff adds pagination params for all groups: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then `group.users...limit(limit)` with no max clamp. This makes it possible for a caller to request an arbitrarily large `limit`, potentially causing heavy DB/serialization work (resource-exhaustion risk). The finding is directly supported by the new code path in `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members` splits an admin-supplied `usernames` string on commas with no cap on count, causing one `User.find_by_username` query per entry; only self-DoS by an already-privileged admin, negligible risk

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop `User.find_by_username(username)` (one query per comma-separated entry) with no cap/limit on how many usernames can be supplied. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/scalability concern (potential self-DoS by an admin), but it’s not a correctness failure in normal use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:88 — xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "..."` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` invoke the controller action directly via a params hash and never resolve through config/routes.rb, so these specs would still pass even if the route definitions in config/routes.rb were wrong; verified empirically with actionpack 4.1.16 that the current bare `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` / `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` declarations inside `resources :groups do ... end` do correctly nest as `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`, matching group.js's `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json` calls, so the route itself is NOT currently broken, but the test suite provides no safety net against a future regression in that route wiring

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new admin routes for group membership (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` inside `resources :groups` in `config/routes.rb`) and adds controller specs that hit `:add_members` / `:remove_member` directly via `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: ...` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: ...`. Those controller specs do not exercise route recognition/generation, so they would still pass even if the route wiring/path were changed or broken. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap around newly introduced route behavior, not a functional defect in the current code.
